summary: Nora can read stickers on Signal and Discord, instead of the chat just saying `[sticker]`.
details: A sticker's bytes are taken into her own custody and described once by a bounded vision call, so she can see what a sticker sent as a conversational booster actually depicts and read it beside the messages around it.
Descriptions are deduplicated by the sticker's own identity and by content, so a repeat sticker — even under a different pack, or on the other platform — costs nothing.
A sticker sent WITH a caption now appears in the transcript at all. Previously the caption was recorded and the sticker itself was dropped entirely.
limitations: Off by default (`media.sticker_descriptions`). Stickers only — photos, voice notes and video are still described only when Nora chooses to look at them herself.
Discord's lottie (JSON animation) stickers are held but not described — there is nothing for a vision model to read. png/apng/gif stickers, including Discord's animated ones, ARE described.

A repeat sticker skips the vision call, not the platform fetch: a content-level hit (the same art under a new identity) still costs one fetch from the platform, only the identity-level hit is free of both.
Verified against the deployed gateway: the vision model reads an animated WebP sticker correctly, not just its first frame.
